# Mews & GrowthBook
Date: 2026-09-09 | Duration: 53.95000076293945m

## Summary
The team discussed moving experimentation fully in-house by offboarding Spiro by Q1 next year and reducing dependence on limited internal developer capacity. GrowthBook was presented as an AI-first, API-driven platform supporting self-serve experimentation, visual editing, AI-generated variants, server-side and client-side testing, and reduced flicker through its Edge SDK proxy. Payload CMS integration, reusable experimentation blocks, Figma workflows, and HubSpot form editing were considered important for enabling marketing and growth teams to launch tests independently. Native BigQuery and Databricks integrations would support flexible metrics, funnel analysis, and retroactive reporting, while AI-assisted analysis could help teams interpret results. APIs and Claude integration could automate summaries and updates in Confluence and JIRA, with Slack notifications also planned. The current target is 12 experiments per quarter, with potential to scale substantially. Pricing discussions will use estimated seats and monthly sessions, with a pricing review planned for September 23 and budget decisions required in Q4.

## Keywords
CRO, experimentation, AI integration, GrowthBook, Spiro off-boarding, Payload CMS

## Action Items

**Adam Cheal**
Provide monthly website traffic data post-meeting to support GrowthBook pricing and planning (16:22)
Deliver count of user seats who will access experimentation tools to assist GrowthBook pricing discussions (51:36)
Continue working on the statement of work with Spiro regarding off-boarding and potential retainer transition for early 2024 (49:57)

**James Shannon**
Follow up with Ben at Spiro to facilitate discussions and share insights about transitioning experimentation in-house (22:41)
Provide documentation and videos clarifying how to manipulate iframe-embedded HubSpot forms in GrowthBook Visual Editor (34:54)
Share GrowthBook pricing documents for Muse review and schedule a follow-up presentation on September 23rd at 10 AM (51:42)
Send documentation on Edge SDK and flicker reduction techniques discussed during the meeting (13:58)
Deliver a summary write-up of key GrowthBook features and integrations demonstrated during the Visual Editor demo (35:28)
Assist Muse with integration strategies for linking experiment learnings and results to Confluence and JIRA using GrowthBook API and Claude automations (46:28)

**Rémy Marin**
Verify and provide details on GrowthBook’s Slack integration capabilities for experiment notifications (39:52)
Support James Shannon in clarifying UI features that hide or disable iframe form elements in GrowthBook Visual Editor (33:53)

# Mews & GrowthBook Commercials
Date: 2026-09-23 | Duration: 24.56999969482422m

## Summary
The team is preparing a proof of concept for a new A/B testing platform, targeting January 2027 to align with AV Tasty’s contract ending in March. The POC will test visual-editor and server-side workflows, experiment setup speed, ease of use, and measurement using existing GA4 events, with a 30-day opt-out and no financial commitment. GA4 currently tracks demo submissions and thank-you-page visits but is not linked to CRM data; Databricks, Hex, and future HubSpot integration may improve revenue attribution later. Adam Cheal is the primary decision-maker, supported by developers and web product manager James Shannon, while director Tatiana provides final budget approval. Proposed pricing is $75,000 annually for 60 experiments, unlimited users, and enterprise features, with $500 overage experiments; this exceeds the current AV Tasty cost of £31,000 from March and requires a business case. The transition is treated as a critical risk, with analyst engagement, procurement planning, and a dedicated Slack channel proposed to maintain alignment. AI capabilities, server-side testing, self-service workflows, and improved performance are key reasons for considering the change. Sources: 03:50, 05:36, 09:09, 10:50, 14:39, 16:35, 21:27, 22:42.

## Keywords
proof of concept, AB testing, procurement process, conversion tracking, budget approval, server-side experimentation

## Action Items

**Adam Cheal**
Obtain buy-in and approval from director Tatiana for the tool switch and associated budget over the next month (20:05)
Reach out to web analysts after the 2027 planning offsite to discuss the AB testing tool and address any technical questions (22:42)
Continue updating transition plans and project trackers, including procurement and risk plans related to replacing AB Tasty (21:27)

**James Shannon**
Create and share a Slack channel with Adam Cheal to facilitate streamlined communication and reduce meeting frequency (21:41)
Send commercial proposal, pricing details, and diagrams via email to Adam Cheal for internal circulation (22:57)
Provide additional support materials such as decks, conversion rate studies, and case studies to assist Adam Cheal in building the value case for budget approval (18:32)
